title: Source-First Notary Training Posture
coreRule: Use training, handbooks, platform support, association summaries, community answers, and AI as leads. Do not use them as safe harbor.
authorityRule: The controlling legal text, official rule, official agency source, competent-authority source, recipient's published requirement, and transaction evidence must remain visible when they control the route.

examples: court or UPL authority when applicable
sourceHierarchy.use: Controls the legal claim when applicable.
Helps apply or explain the controlling rule, but should not override the law.
Applies the route to the recipient or destination when recipient acceptance matters.
Shows how the source applies to the actual transaction.
Evidence of what someone claims, sells, teaches, or repeats. Not legal authority or route proof.

trainingQuestion: What official source proves that for this jurisdiction, transaction date, notarial act, identity method, document type, output format, and recipient route?

confidenceTrap.summary: Confidence gained from answering beginner questions is not the same as source authority.
pattern: A person learns enough to answer beginner questions.
The people nearby mostly ask beginner questions.
The person begins to feel like an authority.
The same community, platform, trainer, or association reinforces the original rule.
If the original rule was incomplete, the wrong answer becomes more confident over time.
confidenceTrap.sourceQualityRule: The issue is not whether the person is sincere. The issue is whether the answer still has source authority when the transaction is challenged.

handbookAndSummaryBoundary: Official handbooks and agency explainers can be useful, but they can simplify a statute or leave out definitions, exceptions, or cross-references. Use summaries to find the source, then inspect the source.

aiBoundary.rule: AI can make public law easier to read and navigate, but it must not silently compress away the detail that matters.
sourceFirstAiAnswerShould: cite the official source or source index
preserve transaction date when it matters
keep Notary Geek interpretation separate from official text
avoid turning platform, trainer, market, or association language into legal authority
say when a source needs refresh before a transaction-specific answer

mustAskBeforeRepeatingTrainingAnswer: What exact act is being requested?
What law or official source controls that act?
What words in the source actually matter?
Are there definitions, exceptions, or cross-references?
What evidence would remain if the act, route, platform, recipient, or apostille were challenged later?
mustNotSay: A trainer said it, so it is safe.
A platform allows it, so it is lawful.
Everyone does it, so the route is proven.
The handbook summary is always the whole law.
AI summarized the rule, so the controlling text no longer matters.
Sincerity or experience is the same as source authority.
failureSignals: training statement repeated without source class or transaction-date check
platform workflow treated as legal authority
official handbook or agency summary treated as if no statute, definition, exception, or cross-reference can change it
private association or market habit treated as public notarial authority
AI answer compresses away source text and uncertainty
confidence, reputation, or beginner-question fluency treated as evidence
